column2: [Root.Spouse.GetFirstName] stands in the doorway of your bedchamber with [Root.Spouse.GetHerHis] arms folded. "I have had the servants make up the east rooms for me," [Root.Spouse.GetSheHe] says. "You toss and groan all night, you stink of the sickroom, and frankly I can no longer bear it. From now on we sleep apart."
Gladly. Your snoring was no better.
Stay. Let me remind you why you married me.
As you wish, my dear.

Your heir is grown, the succession is safe, and the woman beside you has given you nothing in all these years but cold looks. The priests of [Root.Religion.GetName] do not love a lord who casts off his wife, but they love a full treasury more, and there are ways. You could put [Root.Spouse.GetFirstName] aside and be done with [Root.Spouse.GetHerHim].
Get out of my sight. We are finished.
One more try. For the children's sake.

[From.GetFirstName] has cast you out like a kitchen drudge, after all the years you gave [From.GetHerHim]. But the temple swore you to each other before the god, and the temple does not forget its oaths. A letter to the high priest might yet bring [From.GetHerHim] to heel.
Let the temple judge [From.GetHerHim]!
Your former wife may appeal to the temple

A stern letter has come from the high priest. [From.GetFirstName] has appealed to the temple, and the temple sides with [From.GetHerHim]: what was sworn before the god cannot be undone by a lord's temper. Take [From.GetHerHim] back, the letter says, or answer for it.
Very well. Bring [From.GetHerHim] home.
Let the priests rage. I will not.
[From.GetFirstName] appeals to the temple

Your husband's heir [poisoned_heir.GetFirstName] is a sturdy, smiling child, born of another woman, and every day [poisoned_heir.GetSheHe] lives your own child stands one step further from the throne. The herb-wife in the lower town sells powders for rats. Nobody would wonder much if a child fell sick.
A pinch in [poisoned_heir.GetHerHis] cup...
No. I will not murder a child.

Your heir [poisoned_heir.GetFirstName] has fallen ill, and the physicians do not like the look of it. Neither do you. [From.GetFirstName] has been unusually attentive to the child's meals of late, and [From.GetSheHe] has never hidden how much [From.GetSheHe] wants [From.GetHerHis] own child to rule after you.
Throw [From.GetHerHim] in the dungeon!
Fetch the headsman.
I cannot prove it. Let it go.
Your husband may suspect you

[target_courtier.GetFirstName] was in the kitchens the night you visited them, and now [target_courtier.GetSheHe] watches you with a knowing look. Sooner or later [target_courtier.GetSheHe] will say something to your husband, unless you do something first.
Let [target_courtier.GetHerHim] talk. Nobody listens to servants.
A purse of gold buys a great deal of silence.
There is more of that powder left.
Someone may have seen you

Your heir [poisoned_heir.GetFirstName] is dead, and the physicians found a bitter smell in [poisoned_heir.GetHerHis] mouth. You know who stands to gain. [From.GetFirstName] wept at the graveside, but [From.GetHerHis] eyes were dry.
Your husband may accuse you of murder

[target_courtier.GetFirstName] has been whispering in corners since the funeral. The word is "poison", and the name that goes with it is yours. If the whispers reach your husband you will hang for it.
Someone may have seen you
The guards came at dawn. Now you sit on damp straw in the dark below the keep, and the only sound is the dripping of water and the rats. This is not how it was supposed to end.
I will not die down here!
Thrown into the dungeon

Your [From.GetHusbandWife] has spared you, but before the whole court [From.GetSheHe] named you a poisoner and then forgave you, which is worse. Every cup you are handed now comes with a sidelong look.
They will forget, in time.
Pardoned, but shamed

First your heir [poisoned_heir.GetFirstName] sickened, and now the courtier [target_courtier.GetFirstName], who was asking questions about it, has fallen ill the same way. Two cups, one poisoner, and the trail leads to [From.GetFirstName].
Your husband may learn everything

Your son lies pale and sweating in his bed, and the physicians shrug. But you are not a fool. Your wife [Root.Spouse.GetFirstName] has a busy mind and a sharp tongue, and you have seen how [Root.Spouse.GetSheHe] looks at the boy who stands between [Root.Spouse.GetHerHis] children and your throne.
Guards! Take [Root.Spouse.GetHerHim] below!
The headsman will have [Root.Spouse.GetHerHis] head.
I have no proof... this time.

You are sick and weak and getting no better, and every meal you eat is brought by [Root.Spouse.GetFirstName]. You have caught [Root.Spouse.GetHerHim] watching you drink. What a [Root.Spouse.GetHusbandWife] gains from a dead lord is no secret.
Lock [Root.Spouse.GetHerHim] away before [Root.Spouse.GetSheHe] finishes it!
Off with [Root.Spouse.GetHerHis] head!
I am being foolish. Forgive me.

You have known for a long time, but now there is no pretending. Your husband [Root.Spouse.GetFirstName] does not come to your bed because he prefers the company of men, and the court is beginning to notice. You have given him an heir, which is all the world asks of a marriage. The rest is up to you.
It is his business. I will say nothing.
Let a few words drop in the right ears...
Ask him to give me more of his time.

Your wife [From.GetFirstName] has been talking. Now every page and washerwoman in the castle is giggling about who shares your bed, and your vassals look at you with a smirk they think you cannot see.
[From.GetSheHe] will regret this.
Your husband will hear the rumours

[From.GetFirstName] has asked you, quietly and without accusation, to spend more of your evenings with [From.GetHerHim]. [From.GetSheHe] does not ask you to change who you are. [From.GetSheHe] only asks not to be alone.
Of course. You deserve that much.
My evenings are my own.
Your husband will answer
Your husband [From.GetFirstName] has given you an answer.
He will spend more time with me. Good.
He refused. I expected nothing else.
He agrees
He refuses
[From.GetFirstName] knows who has been spreading the stories. [From.GetSheHe] said nothing at dinner, but [From.GetSheHe] looked straight at you while [From.GetSheHe] said it, and the whole hall saw.
Let [From.GetHerHim] glare.
Your husband knows you spread the rumours

Days and nights in the cell run together. What keeps you sane is the thought of [outside_spouse.GetFirstName], who loves you and is still free. If anyone in the world would move heaven and earth for you, it is [outside_spouse.GetHerHim].
Beg [prisoner_host.GetTitledFirstName] for mercy.
Smuggle a letter to [outside_spouse.GetFirstName].
There is no hope.

Your prisoner [From.GetTitledFirstName] has been weeping and pleading through the bars for days, swearing that [From.GetHerHis] [outside_spouse.GetHusbandWife] [outside_spouse.GetFirstName] will pay anything at all for [From.GetHerHis] release.
Make an example of [From.GetHerHim].
Let [outside_spouse.GetFirstName] pay, then.
The deepest cell for [From.GetHerHim].
Warn [outside_spouse.GetFirstName] not to try anything.
Your jailer hears your plea
A filthy scrap of parchment reached you through a bribed guard. It is in [From.GetFirstName]'s hand, and it says only: "Save me."
I cannot. Forgive me.
I will go to [prisoner_host.GetTitledFirstName] myself!
Your spouse receives your letter
[prisoner_spouse.GetFirstName] is dead, killed in [prisoner_host.GetTitledFirstName]'s dungeon. You were not there. You could not save [prisoner_spouse.GetHerHim].
I cannot bear it.
[prisoner_host.GetFirstName] will pay for this in blood!
Why [prisoner_spouse.GetHerHim]? Why not someone else?
Your spouse learns of your death
The cell door swings open and the guards stand aside. You are free! [outside_spouse.GetFirstName] did not forget you.
Home, at last.
The prisoner is set free
The guards drag you down, past the cells with windows and the cells with straw, to the deep pit where no light reaches at all.
Gods, no...
The prisoner is thrown into the deep dungeon

[Root.GetTitledFirstName],

I hold your [prisoner_spouse.GetHusbandWife] [prisoner_spouse.GetFirstName], as you know. I am told you mean to plead for [prisoner_spouse.GetHerHim], or worse, to try to free [prisoner_spouse.GetHerHim]. Do not. You will not like what follows.

[From.GetTitledFirstName]
I will do nothing.
I will plead regardless.
The free spouse is warned

[From.GetTitledFirstName] has come to your hall to plead for [From.GetHerHis] [prisoner_spouse.GetHusbandWife] [prisoner_spouse.GetFirstName], whom you hold in your dungeon. [From.GetSheHe] kneels on the flagstones and begs.
Fine. Take [prisoner_spouse.GetHerHim] and go.
The prisoner goes to the deep pit for this.
Hang the prisoner. Let [From.GetHerHim] watch.
You plead with the jailer
You plead anyway

[annoying_courtier.GetTitledFirstName], who sits on your husband's council, has been making jokes at your expense, loudly and where you can hear them: how little you know of the realm, how you should stick to your embroidery. The court laughs along.
Perhaps [annoying_courtier.GetSheHe] has a point.
My husband will have [annoying_courtier.GetHerHim] dismissed.
Two can play at mockery.

[From.GetFirstName] is furious. [annoying_courtier.GetTitledFirstName] has insulted [From.GetHerHim] in front of the whole court, [From.GetSheHe] says, and [From.GetSheHe] wants [annoying_courtier.GetHerHim] off your council by nightfall.
Then [annoying_courtier.GetSheHe] is dismissed.
I need [annoying_courtier.GetHerHim]. Learn to laugh it off.
Your husband must decide

[annoying_courtier.GetTitledFirstName] has come to you red-faced. Your wife [From.GetFirstName] mocked [annoying_courtier.GetHerHim] before the whole court, [annoying_courtier.GetSheHe] says, and [annoying_courtier.GetSheHe] will not serve where [annoying_courtier.GetSheHe] is made a fool.
My wife went too far. I apologise for her.
You started it. Now you can finish it.
Your husband hears of it

You are walking by the river with [chosen_courtier.GetTitledFirstName], who has not stopped talking since you left the castle. The bank is steep, the water is cold and fast and deep, and [chosen_courtier.GetSheHe] is standing very near the edge.
Oops.
Do be quiet for once.
Pray to the gods for patience.

It all happened so fast. One little push, a splash, a cry, and the river swallowed [chosen_courtier.GetTitledFirstName] whole. By the time the guards came running, there was nothing left to see but ripples. Now the whole court is staring at you.
I am so sorry! It was an accident!
[chosen_courtier.GetSheHe] slipped. I swear it.
If only I had caught [chosen_courtier.GetHerHis] hand!
Good riddance.
The courtier may drown

A push, a splash and a great deal of thrashing, and then [chosen_courtier.GetTitledFirstName] crawled out onto the bank, soaked to the skin and coughing up river water. [chosen_courtier.GetSheHe] knows exactly what happened, and so will everyone else by supper.
Curses.
The courtier may survive
A jeweller from Marienburg has come to court with a casket of rings, brooches and necklaces. [Root.Spouse.GetFirstName] has been cool towards you lately, and nothing warms a heart like gold.
A pretty brooch will do.
A fine necklace of pearls.
The best piece, and a night to remember.
Away with the man. I am not made of gold.

The horse-copers are at the castle gate with their spring stock, and [my_spouse.GetFirstName] has been looking at them from the window. A fine horse would make a handsome gift, and a ride out together even more so.
A gentle old mare.
The finest palfrey they have.
The palfrey, and a long ride, just the two of us.
Horses cost money. No.
Neigh.
The falconers have brought in a young peregrine, fierce and fast. [my_spouse.GetFirstName] has always admired the hunt, and a bird of [my_spouse.GetHerHis] own would delight [my_spouse.GetHerHim].

The falconers have brought in a young peregrine, fierce and fast. [my_spouse.GetFirstName] loves to watch it fly, though last time [my_spouse.GetSheHe] tried to feed it porridge. Still, a bird of [my_spouse.GetHerHis] own would delight [my_spouse.GetHerHim].
A pair of fine gloves for the hunt.
The peregrine, and a falconer to train [my_spouse.GetHerHim].
Nonsense. Birds are for eating.

You have always found the endless courtesies of diplomacy tiresome, and it shows in your letters. [Root.Spouse.GetFirstName] has a gift for it. "Let me help," [Root.Spouse.GetSheHe] says. "Show me your letters before you send them, and I will show you how to win a man without his ever noticing."
Very well. Teach me.
I need no help from you.

Your last war was a near thing, and everyone at court knows it. [Root.Spouse.GetFirstName] reads the old campaign books by candlelight and understands them better than most of your captains. "Let me go over the maps with you," [Root.Spouse.GetSheHe] says.
Show me what you see.

The accounts are a mess, the tax-gatherers rob you blind and you cannot make head or tail of the ledgers. [Root.Spouse.GetFirstName] can. "Give me an evening a week with the books," [Root.Spouse.GetSheHe] says, "and you will be a richer lord by midsummer."
The books are yours.
The court is full of whisperers and you hear none of it. [Root.Spouse.GetFirstName] hears everything. "You trust far too easily," [Root.Spouse.GetSheHe] says. "Let me teach you how to listen."
Teach me, then.

You have never had much patience for books, and the priests at your table know it. [Root.Spouse.GetFirstName] has read more than most of them. "Read with me in the evenings," [Root.Spouse.GetSheHe] says. "A lord should know more of the world than what his priests tell him."

You have never had much patience for books, and the scholars of the court know it. [Root.Spouse.GetFirstName] has read the great works of Araby's sages and astrologers. "Read with me in the evenings," [Root.Spouse.GetSheHe] says. "The wise rule. The ignorant are ruled."
Let us read together.

[new_councillor.GetTitledFirstName] is clever, loyal and devoted to you, and [new_councillor.GetSheHe] would do far better on your husband's council than the fool who sits there now. A word in your husband's ear could make it so, and a councillor who owes you the seat is worth a great deal.
I will speak to my husband tonight.
Better not to meddle.

Your wife [From.GetFirstName] has been praising [new_councillor.GetTitledFirstName] all evening, how clever [new_councillor.GetSheHe] is, how much better [new_councillor.GetSheHe] would serve on your council than the one who sits there now.

Your wife [From.GetFirstName] has been praising [new_councillor.GetTitledFirstName] all evening, how clever [new_councillor.GetSheHe] is, how much better [new_councillor.GetSheHe] would serve on your council. Half the court whispers that [new_councillor.GetSheHe] warms more than [From.GetHerHis] ear, but perhaps that is only gossip.
Very well, [new_councillor.GetSheHe] shall have the seat.
My council is my own affair.
Your husband will decide
Your husband [From.GetFirstName] has made up his mind about [new_councillor.GetTitledFirstName].
[new_councillor.GetSheHe] has the seat. Splendid.
He refused me. I will remember that.
He gives the seat
He refuses

Your husband is old, his seed is weak, and the cradle in your chamber stays empty year after year. Yet there are men at court who look at you with longing, and one of them is young and handsome and would do anything you asked. Your husband need never know.
It is done before I can think better of it.
No. I made a vow.
You are with child. You know whose it is, and it is not your husband's. What will you tell him?
Nothing. Let him think it is his.
The truth.
That I was forced.
[From.GetFirstName] blushes as [From.GetSheHe] tells you the news: [From.GetSheHe] is with child! After so many barren years, the gods have smiled on you at last.
The gods be praised!
You tell your husband the child is his

[From.GetFirstName] is with child, and [From.GetSheHe] has told you the truth, weeping: the father is [sire_bastard.GetTitledFirstName]. You can raise the child as your own and hide the shame, or you can let the world see your anger.
The child is mine. That is all anyone will know.
The child is mine, but the man will pay.
Both of them will pay!
You tell your husband the truth

[From.GetFirstName] is with child, and [From.GetSheHe] has told you, shaking, that [sire_bastard.GetTitledFirstName] forced himself on [From.GetHerHim]. [From.GetSheHe] cannot quite meet your eyes as [From.GetSheHe] says it.
You tell your husband you were forced
[sire_bastard.GetTitledFirstName] stands before you in chains. What is to be done with [sire_bastard.GetHerHim]?
The dungeon.
The rope.
Exile. Out of my lands for good.
Let [sire_bastard.GetHerHim] go. It is over.
The courtier is punished
[sire_bastard.GetTitledFirstName] and [cuckoo_mother.GetFirstName] stand before you in chains, side by side, and neither will look at the other. What is to be done with them?
The dungeon for both.
The rope for both.
Exile for both.
Spare [cuckoo_mother.GetHerHim]. Deal with [sire_bastard.GetHerHim].
Both are punished

[Root.Spouse.GetFirstName] trails after you from room to room like a lost puppy. "I am SO bored," [Root.Spouse.GetSheHe] wails. "You are always busy and there is nothing to do here and nobody to talk to. Can we not go riding? Or have a feast? Or anything at all?"
Oh, very well. Just this once.
Go and make a friend. [target_courtier.GetFirstName] seems nice.
Your husband has told you to make friends with [target_courtier.GetTitledFirstName]. Well, you will. But how?
A boat on the river.
A picnic in the orchard.
A day's hunting.
A grand dinner.
This is hopeless. I give up.
Your wife looks for a friend
It was a lovely day. You laughed until your sides ached, and [target_courtier.GetTitledFirstName] laughed with you. You think you have made a friend.
A friend at last!
It was a disaster. It rained, or the food was bad, or you said entirely the wrong thing, and [target_courtier.GetTitledFirstName] left early with a very polite smile.
Let us try something else.
We were never meant to be friends.
Your husband [Root.Spouse.GetFirstName] is not as young as he was, but you are, and the nights are long. Tonight you mean to make the most of one.
A wild ride he will not forget.
Show him who rules the bedchamber.
Gently, now.
Sweet and slow.
Your young wife [From.GetFirstName] was a storm last night. You have not felt like this in years. Your heart pounded like a war drum, and it is still pounding now.
By the gods, I feel twenty again!
A wild night
A fierce night
Your wife [From.GetFirstName] was so tender last night that you lay awake for hours afterwards, smiling at the ceiling like a boy.
I am a lucky man.
A gentle night
A sweet night
Your husband's heart gave out in the middle of the night, in your arms. The physicians say it was a good death, as deaths go. The court is already whispering, and some of the whispers are laughing.
I loved him to death...
His heart may give out

Year after year your husband [Root.Spouse.GetFirstName] comes to your bed, and year after year nothing comes of it. It is not you, you are sure of it. But there are young men at court who would be glad to prove the point, and a child is a child, whoever the father is.
One night. Nobody needs to know.
I will stay faithful.
